..
An active weather pattern will persist across the Marianas beginning
this evening through Saturday night before tapering down on Labor 
Day. A surface trough associated with Invest 97W to the west and a 
col to the east places the region within an unsettled convergence 
zone. As seen on satellite, westerly flow is buckling against the 
frontmost quadrants of the col, and as the col continues moving west-
northwest, numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms with possible
locally heavy showers are expected Saturday and Saturday night, 
potentially heavier over Saipan and Tinian. Scatterometry depicts 
moderate to fresh southwesterlies which will taper down to gentle to 
moderate after tonight, with occasional convective gusts up to 25 mph
possible. Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms are forecasted
through Labor Day, followed by a potential dry spell through the 
remainder of next week.

Marine...
Model guidance suggests the elevated westerly swell to linger 
slightly longer than previously anticipated, so surf along west-
facing reefs will remain 7 to 9 ft through tonight. As such, there is
a high risk of rip currents, so both hazards were extended until 4 AM
ChST Saturday. Surf is expected to drop below hazardous levels by
this time, but this will continue to be monitored overnight. Combined
seas are 6 to 8 ft and will drop by a foot or two through the next
week.

Tropical Systems...
Invest 97W is located about 370 miles south-southwest of Iwo To  
near 19.2N 138.3E and is moving northwest. The Joint Typhoon Warning
Center (JTWC) has upgraded 97W to high, and has issued a Tropical
Cyclone Formation Alert (TCFA). This means that development into a 
significant tropical cyclone (tropical depression) is likely within 
the next 24 hours. Invest 97W is now showing a tightly closed Low- 
Level Circulation Center (LLCC). 97W is expected to move northwest 
over the next few days as it continues to consolidate. Invest 97W 
will have no direct impact on Micronesia nor the Marianas.

For more information on Invest 97W, see bulletins issued by JTWC
under WMO headers WTPN21 PGTW and ABPW10 PGTW.

Eastern Micronesia...
A band of convergence to the southwest of the monsoon trough is
generating scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms across
Pohnpei and Kosrae this evening. This area of convection looks to
slowly move away from Kosrae through the night, with isolated 
showers expected over the island by midnight. Convection will linger
at Pohnpei a bit longer as the monsoon trough slowly drifts west, 
pushing the band of convergence toward Chuuk. A dry pattern will 
then dominate at both Pohnpei and Kosrae into the beginning of next 
week. The dry pattern at Majuro looks to continue through the
weekend. Early next week, the monsoon pattern looks to become a bit
more active, with a weak surge developing, bringing increased 
showers and thunderstorms to Majuro Monday, with the convection
increasing westward toward Kosrae and Pohnpei by Tuesday.

Light to gentle winds will prevail through the weekend and into the
beginning of next week. Then a weak monsoon surge will bring gentle
to moderate winds to Majuro and Pohnpei, with moderate to fresh winds
at Kosrae. Seas will become a bit choppy, with a chaotic wave pattern
over the region. Seas will remain fairly low, however, peaking at
around 5 to 6 feet near the middle of next week.

Western Micronesia...
Overall, the region remain south and west of the monsoon trough, 
that stretches across the far northern Marianas and curves
southeastward into eastern Micronesia. Fairly dry conditions 
persists across Yap and Palau through early next week. Showers are 
building across northeastern Chuuk State, tied to the increase in 
northwesterly convergence towards the monsoon trough and disturbance 
in eastern Micronesia. This band of convergence gradually shifts 
westward in the coming days, producing scattered showers and isolated
thunderstorms across Chuuk through the weekend, then shower coverage
slightly lowers to isolated to scattered Monday and Tuesday as the 
feature moves farther westward, bringing scattered showers to Yap 
around Wednesday. Southwesterly convergence alongside the monsoon 
trough begins to set up across Chuuk around Wednesday as well, 
bringing another increase in scattered showers and isolated 
thunderstorms towards the latter half of next week. 

Latest altimetry data shows combined seas of 3 to 5 feet near Palau
and 4 to 6 feet across Yap and Chuuk coastal waters. Combined seas
are expected to subside another foot as westerly swells diminish
slightly. Light to gentle winds persists over the next several days
with an increase in gentle to moderate southwesterly winds at Chuuk 
towards the latter half of next week.
